implementation: Implemented pure fail-closed state migration: explicit source/target tensor mapping requires a non-empty user semantic_reason; exact shape/dtype only; unknown/duplicate/unaccounted state rejected.
Target state is copied before mutation; preserve/reset/drop accounting is exact. Reports optimizer reset and rejects non-Tensor custom extra state without an explicit adapter.

Training checkpoints persist shared parameter/buffer alias groups. Migration requires full one-to-one mapping of each preserved alias group to an identical target group; topology changes must reset/drop the whole groups. A source checkpoint without alias evidence fails closed.

CLI supports `train --migrate-from RUN_ID --migration-plan FILE`; a verified parent checkpoint seeds a new step-zero child checkpoint and report, while optimizer state resets and the parent checkpoint remains immutable.
Added migration module to Rust embedded worker assets and public edit package exports.

validation.result: passed 2/2: explicit tensor semantics/accounting planner and full parent->child CLI migration. The integration test covers tied alias preservation, tied-to-untied refusal, immutable parent checkpoint, optimizer reset, child resume, legacy checkpoint physically missing alias metadata rejected before child checkpoint publication, and failure/no-half-publish.

passed 2/2. The CLI integration creates a real trained parent checkpoint, migrates exact tensors with tied aliases into a child, verifies parent bytes are unchanged and optimizer state resets, inspects checkpoint alias metadata, resumes the child, and rejects missing alias metadata, tied-to-untied preservation, and unaccounted migration plans without publishing child latest.json.

limitations: Tensor transforms such as slicing, reshaping, widening, narrowing, merging, splitting, or dtype conversion have no adapter and fail closed; supported migration is exact shape/dtype one-to-one copy with an explicit semantic reason.
Non-Tensor custom extra state has no migration adapter and fails closed. Optimizer, scheduler, scaler, and step state do not transfer; the child starts at step zero with fresh optimizer state.

Preserving a shared parameter/buffer requires matching complete source and target alias groups. Topology changes can only reset the whole target alias group and drop the whole source group; checkpoints without alias-group evidence cannot be migration sources.

Failure publication evidence covers migration validation failures before child checkpoint publication. A successfully migrated step-zero checkpoint is intentionally durable so a later training failure can resume from it.
